key_claims: Regular stair climbers were 39% less likely to die from cardiovascular disease.
Regular stair climbers were 24% less likely to die from any cause.
Regular stair climbing was associated with lower risks of heart attack, stroke, and heart failure.
The analysis included data from more than 480,000 people from nine high-quality studies.
Participants were followed for a median of 14 years.
limitations: Stair climbing may not be suitable for everyone, especially those with mobility limitations or joint conditions.
The ideal 'dose' of stair climbing is not yet determined.
Future studies should use wearable technology to track physical activity more precisely.
what_not_to_say: Stair climbing causes a 39% reduction in cardiovascular death risk.
Climbing six flights of stairs daily provides the greatest benefit.
Stair climbing is recommended for everyone.
The study proves that stair climbing prevents cardiovascular disease.
